primary_claim: Extending the Local Learning Coefficient from Singular Learning Theory to per-input granularity (the per-sample LLC, or pLLC) distinguishes memorized inputs from generalizing inputs (classifying mislabeled MNIST examples with over 0.95 accuracy from pLLC traces), reveals interpretable structure across temperatures in a modular-arithmetic transformer, and scales to flagging memorized 'trojan' inputs in a fine-tuned language model.

effect.metric: accuracy classifying mislabeled/memorized MNIST examples using a linear regression on pLLC traces
effect.value: over 0.95 overall accuracy, 0.96 precision for mislabeled examples

contradicts_or_qualifies: Hessian-based methods linking memorization to sharp loss-landscape directions suffer from parameter transformation sensitivity and are limited to local quadratic approximations, and NTK/influence-function approaches remain largely theoretical or face computational challenges, which the pLLC approach aims to avoid
stated_future_work: studying the effect of temperature in greater detail on the clustering of the modular addition and multiplication model
more work needed to show how often the spiral pattern appears and if it changes from run to run
experiments to figure out how clusters should be interpreted, and whether mech interp is needed to explain them
find examples of clusters which correspond to circuits already known to exist, e.g. induction heads
extend to more subtle memorization patterns, e.g. setups from Anthropic's sleeper agents paper or the Emergent Misalignment paper
limitations_stated: while it appears likely the patterns revealed by pLLC analysis are telling us something about model structure, establishing causal connections will require further interventional studies
we haven't learned anything about how any circuitry in the model is 'actually' implemented (we haven't done anything mechanistic)
how much information a trace contains about circuits below its temperature-set efficiency cutoff is unclear
for the trojans tested, which contain obvious out-of-distribution patterns, other detection methods such as per-sample gradients can also be effective
quote: mislabeled examples have significantly higher pLLC values, indicating that they rely on more fragile, input-specific circuits than normal examples
